title: Nim Counts the Lanterns
blurb: Eight sleepy lights, and a moth who helps.
pages: Aida steps into the lantern grove. The lights are sleepy, not spooky. Nim the moth lands on her hat, right beside the pink lily. Four lanterns hang on this branch, and four hang on that one.
Aida lifts her star wand. One lantern wakes. Two. Three. Four. That is one group of four. Nim flutters across the path. The other branch wakes too. Another group of four.
Four and four. Aida holds up her fingers and counts them together. Eight lanterns, all glowing a warm gold. The path looks soft, like evening milk. Nim draws a tiny circle and waits.

If two more lanterns hung on the gate, how many would that be? Aida smiles. Eight and two is ten. The gate lights blink awake, as if they were listening. She and Nim walk on, counting their steps in twos.

title: Even Sips
blurb: Six cups of petal tea, shared fairly.
pages: The cottage kettle hums a friendly hum. Three little bottles sit on the step. Aida and Nim peer into the pot. There are six cups of petal tea, and it smells like warm berries.
Aida pours slowly. One cup for the step. One cup for Nim's leaf. One cup for herself. Then she does it again. Two each. Two and two and two.
A frog-shaped spoon clinks, and Aida laughs. If a friend came, six cups shared by three friends would still be two each. They already did that. Nim looks very pleased with the middle cup.
The bottles glow pink, gold, and green. Aida lines them up. First, second, third. Nim rests on the second bottle, the one in the middle. They leave the step tidy, and the window shines them onward.

title: A Bright Hush
blurb: Five blue crystals and five gold ones.
pages: The cave is quiet and bright, like a room of candles. Crystals grow in soft blues and golds. Aida holds Nim in her cupped hands. Let's see how many are blue, she says, and her voice stays small.
On the left, the blue crystals are one, two, three, four, five. On the right, the gold crystals are one, two, three, four, five too. Five and five. Nim's wings make a papery flutter.
Aida puts her hands together. Ten crystals, from here. A drop of water goes plink, like a tiny bell, not a fright. She likes grouping them in fives, because five is an easy handful.

One crystal is taller than the rest. If the tall one is first, and she hops two ahead, she lands on the third. She touches it gently. It answers with a calm glow. They sit on a smooth stone and listen to the hush.

title: The Kind Clock
blurb: Eight o'clock, and six stars in two rows.
pages: The observatory roof is open to a mild night. Stars look like spilled sugar. Aida finds the garden clock. The short hand is near the eight, and the long hand is on the twelve. That is eight o'clock.
A pale feather has drifted in from the tower. Aida thinks about the long hand. When it walks all the way to the six, that is half past. Half past eight. Nim does not cover the hands.
They look up together. Three stars in a row, and three more in another row. Aida draws the rows with her wand. Three and three is six. A little rectangle of stars.
One moon. One clock. Six stars they chose to count. One and one and six makes a night that feels full, Aida says. They leave the roof open, so the stars can breathe, and walk down the warm steps.

title: Pebble's Hops
blurb: A frog, six pads, and a hop-rest pattern.
pages: Lily pads float like green coins. Pebble the frog blinks a friendly blink. I can hop, he says. Aida kneels so she is not tall. Nim rides the brim of her hat and stays very quiet.
Pebble hops to the first pad, then the second, then the third. Three hops, Aida counts. If you hop three more, you will be on pad six. Pebble tries. Four, five, six. He looks proud, in a quiet way.
Two pads wear two flowers each. Two groups of two flowers. That is four flowers. Aida does not pick them. She only counts, and the pond holds the moon without breaking it.
Pebble's jumps make a pattern. Hop, rest, hop, rest. It starts again with hop. Aida names it softly. They whisper goodnight to the lilies and take the long path, so nobody has to rush.

title: A Sprout's Measure
pages: The greenhouse is warm glass and the smell of leaves. A sprout stands in a pot. Aida kneels with a ribbon. We can measure you kindly, she says. Nim holds the ribbon's end, very seriously, for a moth.
The first sprout is as tall as four of Aida's fingers. Four finger-lengths. The sprout beside it is two fingers tall. The first is taller. Four is more than two.
She lines up three pots. The heights go two, then four, then six fingers. They grow by two each time. Two, four, six. Like even steps along the bench.

The watering can holds three sips for each pot, and there are three pots. She gives one sip, then another, then a third. The glass fogs with happy warmth. They leave the door a little open, so the sprouts can taste the garden air.

title: Teacup's Books
blurb: Ten books, in fives or in twos.
pages: The tower stairs are round and friendly. Teacup the owl blinks from a stack of books. We should make them tidy, Aida says. Nim lands on a bookmark and waits.

There are ten small books. Aida makes two piles of five. Five and five is ten. Teacup nods, which is a very slow nod. Or five piles of two, Aida says, and she tries. Two, two, two, two, two. Still ten.
A star wand leans by the window. The little clock says three, with the long hand straight up on the twelve. Three o'clock, Teacup. Time for a short rest, not a long one.

They build a stair of books. One, then two on the next step, then three. One plus two plus three is six books in the stair. Teacup hops to the top and hoots like a kettle. Aida laughs, and the tower feels full of good work.

title: Lumen's Circle
blurb: Eight caps, and a circle that matches.
pages: Mushrooms stand in a ring, red caps with pale spots. Lumen the beetle glows like a pocket lantern. Aida steps into the middle with Nim. The ground is soft and mossy, and the evening is kind.
She counts around the circle. Eight mushrooms. If she starts on mushroom one, the one across is mushroom five. She touches them in order. One, two, three, four, five. Lumen waits on the far cap.
Each cap has three spots she can see easily. She counts by threes for two caps. Three and three is six. I will not count every spot today, she tells Lumen. Six is a good start, and the rest can wait.

The ring looks the same if she turns slowly around. This side matches that side. That is a kind of symmetry. They clap once for the circle. Lumen's light stays gold. Aida and Nim take eight soft steps back to the path.

title: Clover's Fair Trade
blurb: Six crystals, and a fox who likes fair sums.
pages: Clover the fox polishes a crystal on the counter. Hello, Aida. A small pile can buy a small thing. Nim peers into a jar. The shop smells like clean wood and berries.

A ribbon costs two crystals. A tiny bell costs three. Aida has six crystals from her walks. Two and three is five. Five is less than six, so she would still have one left. She does not have to buy anything. Clover's tail agrees.

They play a counting game. Four blue crystals and two gold ones. Four plus two is six. Clover sets them in a row. Half of six is three, Aida says, sliding them into two equal groups. Clover looks impressed, in a fox way.

Aida chooses nothing today, and that is allowed. She helps count the bells. One, two, three, four. Even numbers can make pairs. Two pairs. Clover gives Nim a crumb of star-biscuit. The door bell sings once as they leave.

title: Four Pots of Colour
blurb: Blue, gold, pink, and purple, in a pattern.
pages: The nook in the tower is quiet. An easel waits. Four jars sit in a row: blue, gold, pink, and purple. Aida dips a brush. Nim rests by the round window, wings like soft paper.
She paints four stars. One star for each jar. Four jars and four stars. The same number. Then she adds two more stars. Four and two is six stars on the page.
The colours want to repeat. Blue, gold, pink, purple, and then blue again. It starts over. That is a pattern of four. Nim approves by fluttering in a tiny circle above the easel.
She does not have to finish. A half-coloured page is still a good page. I used three jars, she tells Nim. One jar is still waiting. Three and one is four. They close the nook door very gently.
